title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a Grothendieck manuscript note. It is a typed Bourbaki draft (header 'n° 413', page 'A-20'), scanned upside down and kept among the Motifs/Hodge papers, with only the archive pencil foliation '17'. Its content is the formal-group / formal-manifold setup later used in Bourbaki, Groupes et algèbres de Lie, ch. II–III.

Setup:
- A 'noyau formel' (formal kernel) V is modelled on a free module M via a chart φ.
- P̂(V) ≅ completed symmetric algebra (formal power series) is the algebra of formal functions.
- U(V), filtered by U_n(V), is the continuous dual of P̂(V): the module of 'distributions' (of order ≤ n) supported at the origin.
- The transpose φ_* of φ* gives an isomorphism of filtered modules U(V) ≅ S(M). This transports the coalgebra-with-counit ('forme unité') structure of S(M) to U(V).
- Prop. 6 (not shown) gives independence of the chart. Multiplication in P̂(V) is the transpose of the diagonal of U(V).

Definitions on the page:
- U_+(V) is the kernel of the counit, equal to φ_*^{-1}(Σ_{k>0} S^k M).
- The tangent module is T(V) = U_+(V) ∩ U_1(V), equal to φ_*^{-1}(M).
- A formal map f ∈ P̂_+(V;V') (no constant term) induces f_*: U(V) → U(V'). It is filtered and a morphism of counital coalgebras.
- Restricting f_* to T(V) gives the tangent linear map T(f), consistent with n°1 under T(M) = M.
- For V' = the formal kernel of a free M, u ↦ pr_1 ∘ u_* is a bijection from P̂_+(V;M) onto {λ ∈ Hom(U(V), M) : λ|U_0(V) = 0}. This is checked in a chart via 'remarque 2 du n°4'.
- The page ends by starting to define formal maps into a general separated module N.

Purpose: the Cartier-style 'hyperalgebra / distribution' approach to formal groups. A formal group law becomes a bialgebra structure on U(V), and its primitive elements T(V) carry the Lie algebra.

The page has no relation to the surrounding handwritten notes on the cycle class map P_top / P_an / P_alg and factors of 2πi. It is a stray Bourbaki document.
errors: No mathematical errors visible; statements are standard and correct (bijection between formal maps without constant term and linear maps on distributions killing U_0 = scalars).
Archival note: the page is upside down and is a Bourbaki typescript inserted among Grothendieck's motivic notes; it is not part of the argument of pages 16/18.
